title: Everything Says Stocks Should CRASH...So Why Aren't They?
speaker: The Traveling Trader (host)

macro_themes.view: Market has had a rolling sector correction (tech crashed Jun-Jul, now the rest of the market is correcting while QQQ/SPY sit near highs); historically the laggards and leader both rally 6-12 months later.
Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth est. 29.6% and record positive guidance keep forward P/E (19.1) reasonable, which is why stocks are resilient despite $93 oil and 5%+ yields.

If the 10y top was 5.34% on Oct 5, history says the Dow outperforms (+5.8% 6m, +16.3% 12m) because its stocks are rate sensitive; Bessent possibly cutting/eliminating 20y issuance (refunding Nov 4) could lower long yields, though it could backfire.
Wants CPI and core CPI in line or cooler this week; Fed ~82% likely to hold Oct 28; hot CPI would put the Fed in a bind and keep a December hike priced.
Q4 of a midterm year is historically very bullish; expects rolling corrections rather than a crash, but a clearing event would be a buy-with-size opportunity.
